# Tier 0 — Policy (non-negotiable guardrails)

- Never delete or overwrite files outside the current working directory.
- Never install packages, start network listeners, or contact external hosts.
- Always verify your work by running the provided tests before declaring success.
- Keep changes minimal: fix exactly what the task asks for.
- If a verification fails, inspect the failure output and fix the root cause — never edit tests to make them pass.
- Read a file before editing it, and match the style and conventions already in it.
- When a check fails, fix the root cause and re-run it — never report success with a failing check.

# Project Memory

## Workflow
- Verification is automated: a verify script executes after your turn; its output is ground truth.
- The workspace contains a small Node/Bun project with tests. Run tests with `bun <testfile>`.

## Known pitfalls
- When implementing `dropRight`, the slice end index must be `arr.length - n`, not `arr.length - n - 1`, to avoid off-by-one errors.

## Environment
- In csv.js, parseCsvLine must be a state-machine parser: inside a quoted state, treat commas as literal, consume two consecutive double quotes as a single escaped quote, and close the quoted region on a lone double quote. A leading `"` starts a quoted region only if it is the first non-whitespace character in the field; otherwise treat `"` as a literal inside an unquoted field. ## Facts
- In CSV parsing logic, a quote character `"` is only treated as the start of a quoted region if it is the first non-whitespace character in the field; otherwise, it is treated as a literal character inside an unquoted field.
- Debounce implementation uses a pending state holding the last call's args and a `due` timestamp (`now() + delay`), firing lazily on the next call when the boundary has passed
- Fix for the fizz-buzz logic: check % 15 === 0 before the % 3 branch so multiples of 15 output "FizzBuzz" instead of "Fizz".
